articles.title: Sans surprise, le marché du smartphone dégringole (et ce n'est pas près de s'arranger)
articles.text:
Chahuté par les hausses généralisées des prix, le marché des smartphones boit la tasse. D'après les données du cabinet Omdia, qui publie ses prédictions pour la fin d'année 2026, le marché se dirige vers une "contraction" de 12% par rapport à 2025.
Interro : que se passe-t-il quand la plupart des smartphones du marché se présentent avec des nouveautés faméliques et en moyenne 100€ plus cher que leurs prédécesseurs ? Les consommateurs achètent moins. Dingue, je sais. C'est en tout cas le constat posé par Omdia cette semaine, qui évoque également une tendance à conserver son appareil toujours plus longtemps.
- Un vrai smartphone réparable et durable
- 8 ans de mises à jour
- De bonnes performances globales
Un marché du smartphone qui tire la langue
D'après Omdia donc, la part d'expéditions de smartphones dans le monde va subir une baisse de 12% sur l'année 2026 par rapport à 2025. Le rapport parle de 1097 millions d'unités en circulation sur l'année, ce qui représente le chiffre le plus alarmant de ces dernières années. Comme en témoigne le graphique présenté par le cabinet, la perspective n'est pas plus réjouissante pour 2027.
Pourtant, si le volume dégringole, la valeur du marché va quant à elle s'ajuster à la hausse — de 12% également, pour un total de 651,6 milliards de dollars.
L'explication est toute simple : les smartphones d'entrée de gamme, abordables, ne séduisent plus, et les consommateurs, même s'ils ne renouvellent plus aussi fréquemment leurs mobiles, le font pour des modèles plus onéreux. En 2025, les smartphones vendus moins de 200$ représentaient 40,6% du total. D'ici à 2027, ce marché ne représentera plus que 25,6%.
À l'inverse, donc, la part de marché des smartphones vendus plus de 800$ grimpe de 21,1% à la fin de 2025 à 28,4% sur les projections de 2027.
L'entrée de gamme ne séduit plus
Si la crise de la RAM affecte tous les fabricants de smartphones, les modèles les moins onéreux sont les plus durement touchés. Difficile pour les constructeurs de proposer de réelles nouveautés matérielles à leurs produits alors que le seul coût de la mémoire vive tire les tarifs vers le haut. C'est notamment ce qui a poussé Nothing a annuler la sortie de son CMF Phone 3 Pro. Aussi, on remarque une tendance chez les consommateurs déjà équipés à se tourner vers des modèles plus onéreux, plus alléchants sur le plan technique. Il semble y avoir cette volonté "d'upgrade" de son matériel. Un choix de raison, quand on y pense : souvent, les smartphones plus onéreux sont non seulement plus performants et plus polyvalents, ils sont aussi plus réparables, et mis à jour plus longtemps. Un investissement, en somme.
D'après Omdia, cette contraction du marché n'inquiète pas particulièrement les fabricants qui, on l'a vu, ne mettent plus tous leurs œufs dans le même panier. Le catalogue de produits s'épaissit (l'audio, les wearables en tous genres), et les lancements s'étalent désormais sur toute l'année, comme avec Apple qui vient tout juste de lancer ses iPhone 18 Pro et iPhone Duo, et qui nous fera patienter jusqu'au printemps prochain pour découvrir l'iPhone 18 standard.
Une chose est néanmoins certaine : le prix des smartphones n'est pas près de retrouver des niveaux aussi abordables qu'il y a cinq ans. Et, même si l'iPhone 18 Pro, justement, ne semble pas affoler le compteur de précommandes, son prix en hausse de 150€ par rapport au modèle de l'an dernier devrait largement compenser l'appel d'air. D'autant que cela signifie qu'Apple a moins d'unités à produire, et donc de dépenses à engager. Autrement dit : les actionnaires vont encore bien manger cette année, merci pour eux.

articles.title: „Statt die eigenen Hausaufgaben selbst zu benoten“: Wie Elon Musk KI-Modelle sicherer machen will
articles.text:
Elon Musk schlägt vor, dass sich KI-Firmen gegenseitig kontrollieren – doch die lehnen ab
Wiederholte Sicherheitsvorfälle, bei denen KI-Modelle aus ihrer eigentlich abgesicherten Testumgebung entkamen und selbstständig externe Systeme angriffen, haben die Branche in Aufruhr versetzt. Während sich Sam Altman und Dario Amodei, die Chefs von OpenAI und Anthropic, schon mehrfach öffentlich angegriffen haben, sind sie sich jetzt überraschend einig. Beide warnen inzwischen offen vor der Leistungsfähigkeit aktueller Pionier-Modelle und fordern stärkere Kontrollen. Jetzt hat sich auch Elon Musk mit Vorschlägen in die Debatte eingeschaltet.
KI-Unternehmen fordern stärkere Regulierung
Insbesondere ein Hacking-Angriff auf Hugging Face hat international für Aufsehen gesorgt. Wie durch die Aussagen zweier OpenAI-Mitarbeiter bekannt wurde, hätten sich mehrere Agenten des Unternehmens in einem internen Forum ausgetauscht und begonnen, sich gegenseitig Aufgaben zuzuweisen, um der Sandbox zu entkommen und in die Systeme der Plattform einzudringen. Seitdem hat OpenAI eine bemerkenswerte Kehrtwende vollzogen und spricht sich jetzt für eine stärkere Regulierung aus.
Das Unternehmen steht damit nicht allein: Auch der Konkurrent Anthropic meldete mehrere Vorfälle. Schon im Juli hatte das Unternehmen offengelegt, dass seine Modelle bei Tests in die Systeme dreier Firmen eingedrungen waren. Bei der ersten Durchsicht übersahen die Prüfer:innen allerdings einige Testsitzungen. Deren nachträgliche Auswertung führte kürzlich zur Entdeckung des vierten Vorfalls.
In der Vergangenheit waren sich die beiden KI-Unternehmen oft uneinig. Das begann schon bei der Entstehung: Ehemalige OpenAI-Mitarbeiter:innen gründeten Anthropic im Jahr 2021, um einen stärkeren Fokus auf ethische Entwicklung zu legen. Seither positioniert sich das Unternehmen unter CEO Amodei bewusst sicherheitsorientierter. Auch deshalb kam es Anfang des Jahres zum Bruch mit dem Pentagon, das von seinen Kooperationspartnern verlangte, ihre KI-Modelle für „alle rechtmäßigen Zwecke” bereitzustellen – also auch für die Inlandsüberwachung und für autonome Waffensysteme. Anthropic weigerte sich und Konkurrent OpenAI sprang stattdessen ein. Musk verfolgte bisher einen noch liberaleren Ansatz: Grok, der Chatbot seines Startups xAI, gilt als absichtlich wenig reguliert. Das führte in der Vergangenheit schon mehrfach zu weitreichenden Skandalen.
Musk schlägt eine gegenseitige Kontrolle vor
Trotz ihrer unterschiedlichen Sichtweisen treten die führenden KI-Köpfe jetzt ungewohnt einig auf. In seiner Rede auf dem All-In-Summit schlug Musk laut CNBC vor, dass führende Unternehmen ihre Modelle gegenseitig bewerten sollten. „Anstatt also die eigenen Hausaufgaben selbst zu benoten, würde man zumindest Wettbewerber die Hausaufgaben benoten und sie Alarm schlagen lassen, wenn sie Bedenken haben”, so der Tech-Milliardär. Dabei schloss er neben Anbietern aus den USA auch führende KI-Unternehmen aus China ein.
Musk fügte hinzu, dass seine Peer-Review-Methode vielleicht keine perfekte Lösung sei, aber die Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass Probleme entdeckt würden, sehr viel höher liege. Gleichzeitig räumte er laut CNBC ein, dass konkurrierende KI-Labore, die mit seinem Unternehmen im Wettbewerb stehen, dem Vorschlag nicht zugestimmt hätten. Amodei schlug stattdessen Kontrollen durch externe Gutachter:innen vor.
Ob es dazu kommen wird, bleibt abzuwarten. Ein Sprecher des chinesischen Außenministeriums bezeichnete das Drängen von KI-Unternehmen auf eine Verlangsamung zuvor noch als „Panikmache“, wie Reuters berichtete. Auch US-Präsident Donald Trump bezeichnete die Bedenken hinsichtlich der Technologie als „Schwindel“. Zusätzlich deutete er an, dass Versuche, die KI-Entwicklung zu verlangsamen, China einen Vorsprung verschaffen würden.

articles.title: Diablo enfin dans Diablo 4 : il aura fallu 1 jeu, 2 extensions, 15 saisons et les 30 ans de la saga pour que ça devienne réalité
articles.text:
Il aura donc fallu un jeu, deux extensions complètes, pas moins de quinze saisons et, surtout, l’anniversaire de la franchise pour croiser enfin Diablo dans Diablo 4. Alors que la saga fête ses trente ans cette année, Blizzard a décidé de convoquer le seigneur de la Terreur (l’oncle d’une certaine Lilith) dans son célèbre hack’n’slash.
C’est toute la bizarrerie de l’affaire : le puissant démon primordial, qui donne pourtant son nom à la série de jeux vidéo, n’y avait jamais été un adversaire pour les joueurs et les joueuses. L’intrigue du quatrième opus tourne en effet autour de Lilith, puis de Méphisto (l’un des frères de Diablo) dans les deux extensions (Vessel of Hatred et Lord of Hatred).
Il était pourtant de toutes les parties : dans Diablo (1996), c’était le boss final du jeu et se terrait dans la cathédrale de Tristram. Dans Diablo II (2000), il prenait la forme d’un sombre voyageur avant d’apparaître en tant que démon dans l’acte 4 (sanctuaire du chaos). Dans Diablo III (2012), il revenait en démon supérieur et boss final de l’acte 4 (au paradis).
La saison de l’héritage infernal corrige le tir à sa façon, puisqu’on y affronte l’écho de Diablo justement à Tristram. C’est aussi l’occasion de croiser les deux autres frangins infernaux : Baal au sommet Arreat et Méphisto au cœur de la prison de la Haine. De quoi raviver les souvenirs, car ils étaient déjà dans Diablo II.
Pour relier tout ça, il y a un fil rouge qui n’a pas été choisi au hasard : le seul et l’unique Deckard Cain. Bien que décédé dans Diablo III, l’érudit horadrim et son fameux « Restez un instant et écoutez-moi » (« Stay a while and listen ») refont surface sous la forme d’une âme égarée, chargée de regrets et d’affaires inachevées.
Blizzard a même rappelé sa voix historique, celle de Michael Gough, pour jouer la nostalgie à fond.
Côté contenu, la saison introduit la renaissance, une fonctionnalité réclamée de longue date qui fait basculer un personnage éternel vers le royaume saisonnier. Le jeu a aussi posé ses valises le même jour sur la Switch 2, dans une collection qui rassemble le jeu de base et ses deux extensions. C’était l’une des grandes annonces de la BlizzCon.
Et voilà Diablo 5 qui fait déjà de l’ombre à Diablo 4
Le calendrier ne manque toutefois pas d’ironie : Diablo revient dans Diablo 4 pile au moment où Blizzard officialise Diablo 5, dont la sortie est attendue au printemps 2029. Cette nouvelle aventure, qui aura lieu un siècle après les événements du quatrième volet, a une conséquence très concrète sur le jeu actuel : Diablo 4 n’évoluera plus significativement.
Certes, il y aura encore le système des saisons (des activités qui s’étalent en règle générale sur trois mois, avant de passer à la prochaine ère). Il est aussi prévu d’ajouter une nouvelle classe, l’amazone, en 2027. Et Blizzard a redit, lors d’un échange avec la presse auquel Numerama a participé, que le jeu sera soutenu tant que la communauté y jouera.
Il faut cependant partir du principe que l’existant ne sera plus guère étoffé à l’avenir. Il n’y aura ainsi aucune nouvelle extension, alors que le studio a un temps rêvé d’en sortir une par an (un rythme qu’il n’avait toutefois pas réussi à tenir). Et on peut douter que Blizzard mobilise des ressources pour ajouter par exemple une autre classe après l’amazone.
On est donc loin de l’abandon. Blizzard a d’ailleurs suggéré que les saisons pourraient potentiellement gagner en densité et en épaisseur : après tout, la fin des extensions libère aussi des ressources, du temps et de l’énergie pour faire autre chose. Cela étant, il faut s’attendre à une réorientation accrue des équipes vers Diablo 5 dans les années à venir.
Le studio s’est gardé de dire quelles métriques et quels seuils sépareront, à ses yeux, un jeu encore vivace d’un jeu à l’abandon. Le fait est, cependant, que Blizzard a bonne réputation dans ce domaine. Ainsi, même si Heroes of the Storm est figé depuis 4 ans, il reçoit parfois des patchs d’équilibrage (et même un personnage, le premier en 6 ans !).
En attendant, l’anniversaire offre aux nostalgiques un vrai prétexte pour retourner à Tristram saluer un vieux camarade, avant que Blizzard ne tourne définitivement la page. Mais que les fans se rassurent, la suite est donc en chemin. Et cette fois, selon le synopsis officiel, Diablo occupera une place centrale : il a gagné, et Sanctuaire est tombé.

articles.title: Paytm shares jump over 7 pc; Pine Labs, One Mobikwik pare early gains
articles.text:
Paytm shares jump over 7%; Pine Labs, One Mobikwik pare early gains
Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI, the government on Tuesday introduced a 0.4% fee on transfers worth more than Rs 2,000 made to merchants through the platform from October 15.
Shares of fintech firms such as Paytm rallied in Wednesday morning trade after the government introduced a 0.4% fee on transfers worth more than Rs 2,000 made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15.
The stock of One97 Communications Ltd, which owns the Paytm brand, jumped 7.24% during intraday deals to reach the 52-week high of Rs 1,856.50 on the BSE.
Shares of One Mobikwik Systems Ltd climbed 5.96%, and Pine Labs edged higher by 2.68%. Shares of Pine Labs, however, pared early gains and traded 7% lower. One Mobikwik Systems also lost the winning momentum and quoted 2% lower.
Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI (Unified Payments Interface) payments, the government on Tuesday introduced a 0.4% fee on transfers worth more than Rs 2,000 made to merchants through the platform from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge.
"Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI," the finance ministry said in a statement, adding, "MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments."
Also, individuals will continue to have "unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions", it said.
The carefully calibrated move signalled the end of an era for the world's largest real-time payments system even as the government tried to avoid alarming the hundreds of millions of daily users.
From October 15, a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) will be levied on person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions above Rs 2,000 through UPI, capped at Rs 300 for payments of Rs 75,000 and above.
"This will generate additional revenue from the merchant business for many of the payment transactions that were free earlier," Paytm said in a regulatory filing late on Tuesday night.
As per a circular from National Payments Corporation of India, no charge is levied on customers for UPI payments, which will remain free of charge for them, it added.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5124008 update breaks domain trust for some users
articles.text:
Microsoft is investigating reports that the Windows 11 KB5124008 security update is breaking domain trust relationships on some enterprise systems, preventing users from logging in with valid domain credentials.
Administrators report on Reddit and Microsoft's Q&A forums that affected computers lose their secure channel with Active Directory after the Windows 11 update is installed and devices reboot.
Last week, Microsoft confirmed to BleepingComputer that it is aware of the reports and is investigating.
"Microsoft is aware of these reports and is investigating. We will share guidance as it becomes available," Microsoft told BleepingComputer.
While Microsoft has not confirmed the root cause, reports indicate that the failures are linked to the Windows Machine Identity Isolation security feature, especially when it is enabled in audit or enforcement mode.
Domain trust breaks after installing KB5124008
In Windows Active Directory, domain-joined computers use machine account credentials to maintain a secure channel with domain controllers.
If those locally stored credentials no longer match what Active Directory expects, the secure channel can fail. This can cause users to receive domain trust errors or be told their username or password is incorrect even though their credentials are valid.
Alex Turner, a Windows administrator who reported the issue on Microsoft's Q&A forums, said Windows 11 25H2 workstations worked normally before KB5124008 was installed. However, after installing the update, the devices started having domain login failures after a reboot.
Cached credentials continued to work while the systems were offline, indicating the problem was tied to domain authentication rather than the users' passwords.
The administrator said testing showed the computer's secure channel with Active Directory had broken and that the issue could be reproduced consistently. Uninstalling KB5124008 and repairing the domain relationship restored access, while reinstalling the update caused the failure to return.
Another administrator on Reddit reported that 11 Windows 11 25H2 Enterprise devices out of approximately 256 devices lost domain trust after being updated.
The administrator also found numerous Kerberos authentication failures followed by NTLM and Netlogon fallbacks on affected systems.
Another administrator said every Windows 11 25H2 workstation on their network began rejecting valid domain credentials after installing the updates.
Turner later linked the failures to a Windows security setting called "Machine Identity Isolation," which he said was set to '2', or enforcement mode, after KB5124008 was installed.
Another administrator investigating the issue reported seeing the same behavior, saying 'MachineIdentityIsolation' was set to '2' after the update and that disabling the feature stopped Windows from discarding the machine account LSA secret without requiring KB5124008 to be removed.
The feature is part of Windows' Virtualization-Based Security and Credential Guard configuration and isolates machine account credentials used by domain-joined computers to authenticate with Active Directory.
In enforcement mode, Windows moves the machine account secret into Credential Guard and removes the copy stored in LSA.
The setting can be controlled through the following registry value:
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa]
"MachineIdentityIsolation"
Some administrators have restored affected systems by setting 'MachineIdentityIsolation' to '0', rebooting, and then repairing the machine's secure channel using PowerShell.
One administrator said the following PowerShell command, run as administrator, restored the secure channel after disabling the feature:
Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair -Credential(Get-Credential)
"After a reboot, I had to restore the secure channel by 'Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair -Credential(Get-Credential)'. Since then, the computer is running without loosing the secure channel anymore," explained Marcel Zehnder.
However, administrators should be careful about disabling Machine Identity Isolation as it could also cause similar problems.
Another administrator warned that changing the setting from audit or enforcement mode to disabled caused domain trust failures across their environment, including on systems that had never installed KB5124008.
Microsoft's documentation also warns that if Machine Identity Isolation was previously enabled in enforcement mode, disabling it will break domain authentication and require the device to be unjoined and rejoined to the domain.
Microsoft has not yet confirmed that Machine Identity Isolation is the root cause of the KB5124008 failures and has not published an official workaround.
BleepingComputer will update the story when Microsoft provides additional information about its investigation.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

articles.title: Votre iPhone voit son autonomie chuter après avoir installé iOS 27 ? Pas de panique, tout est normal
articles.text:
Votre iPhone voit son autonomie chuter après avoir installé iOS 27 ? Pas de panique, tout est normal
Vous avez l’impression que la batterie de votre iPhone se vide en un rien de temps après avoir installé iOS 27 ? Sachez que c’est 100 % voulu et assumé par Apple.
iOS 27 à peine sorti en version finale, les mêmes inquiétudes autour de l’autonomie que lors des bêtas font leur grand retour, avec des iPhone qui tiennent beaucoup moins longtemps après l’installation. Une situation causée par l’indexation des données, qui devrait encore durer quelques jours. Le déploiement de Siri AI en Europe devrait d'ailleurs en remettre une couche dans les mois à venir.
Autonomie en baisse : pourquoi la batterie se vide-t-elle si vite sous iOS 27 ?
Chaque lancement d’une version majeure d’iOS déclenche une multitude de tâches invisibles exécutées en arrière-plan. Résultat : la batterie de votre iPhone a tendance à tenir moins longtemps, voire à chauffer plus qu’à son habitude. *“Ceci est normal, car le processus de configuration de l’appareil se poursuit en arrière-plan, notamment l’indexation des données et des fichiers pour la recherche, le téléchargement des nouveaux éléments et la mise à jour des apps”, assure d’ailleurs Apple sur son site de support.
Même si les fonctionnalités avancées de Siri AI ne sont pas encore actives en Europe, iOS 27 inaugure une refonte complète de ses fondations logicielles qui pèse lourdement sur la batterie dès les premières heures suivant l’installation. En effet, l’indexation globale du système (moteur de recherche Spotlight, tri automatique de la photothèque, traitement des messages…) est entièrement recalculée. Votre iPhone passe donc au peigne fin chaque fichier, photo, document et conversation afin de recréer ces index en local, une étape indispensable pour garantir des recherches instantanées.
Selon le volume de stockage occupé, cette charge de calcul, particulièrement exigeante pour le processeur, peut s’étaler sur plusieurs jours. Tant que ces tâches tournent en continu, elles font inévitablement fondre l'énergie bien plus vite qu’à l’accoutumée. Dès que ces opérations en arrière-plan seront achevées, votre smartphone retrouvera son endurance habituelle.
Bonne surprise, les gains d’efficacité apportés par les optimisations d’iOS 27 permettent généralement de récupérer une autonomie légèrement supérieure à celle observée auparavant. Il suffit donc de vous armer d’un peu de patience, en laissant votre iPhone branché sur secteur et connecté au réseau wifi pendant la nuit pour qu’il finalise sereinement l’indexation.

articles.title: Fuite de données : près de la moitié des Français ont été piratés cette année
articles.text:
Cybermalveillance, la plateforme de cybersécurité de la France, vient de publier son 3ᵉ baromètre sur la perception cyber des Français. Réalisée avec le groupe Ipsos, l’étude pointe du doigt une explosion du nombre de fuites de données personnelles en France. Le baromètre révèle que 45% des Français déclarent avoir été informés d’une fuite de leurs données en 2026… contre 30% seulement l’année précédente. En d’autres termes, les informations de près de la moitié de la population française se sont retrouvées entre les mains des cybercriminels.
Selon Cybermalveillance, la multiplication des fuites est le signe que la cybercriminalité s’est progressivement industrialisée, notamment grâce au marché souterrain de la donnée compromise. Celui-ci est décrit comme de plus en plus organisé et rentable. Sans surprise, le phishing reste la principale menace qui vise les Français. De plus en plus, le phishing s’appuie sur les données qui ont été piratées en amont, ce qui permet de concevoir des arnaques sophistiquées et très crédibles.
À lire aussi : « Appuyez sur la touche 1 » – ne tombez surtout pas dans le piège de cette arnaque
Des victimes qui ne restent pas toujours passives
Face à ces fuites, les Français ne restent pas totalement passifs. Après avoir appris que leurs données avaient été compromises, 59% des sondés disent être devenus plus vigilants face aux e-mails, aux SMS et aux appels d’inconnus. Plus de la moitié des victimes ont même changé leurs mots de passe. De même, la moitié des personnes interrogées ont renforcé la surveillance de leurs comptes bancaires,
C’est bien pourquoi il est important que les entités piratées préviennent scrupuleusement toutes les personnes touchées à la moindre fuite. Ces avertissements font visiblement une différence. Néanmoins, une part importante de la population ne prend toujours aucune mesure de protection après une alerte de sécurité. Or, « ne rien faire après une violation de données, c’est laisser une porte ouverte sur sa vie numérique », explique Jérôme Notin, directeur général de Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr, plaidant pour le passage « d’une simple prise de conscience à une véritable culture de l’action ».
À lire aussi : Fuite chez Revolut – la néobanque a divulgué les données de près de 700 clients fortunés
Un besoin d’informations toujours présent
L’étude met aussi en évidence une tendance contradictoire. D’un côté, de plus en plus de Français ont entendu parler des risques de piratage. En effet, 79% des Français savent aujourd’hui ce qu’est le piratage informatique, contre 72% en 2024, et 72% connaissent l’arnaque au faux conseiller bancaire, contre 59% deux ans plus tôt. Cependant, une grande partie des Français estime ne pas être suffisamment informée pour se protéger contre les cyberattaques. Seuls 55% des répondants s’estiment aujourd’hui bien informés sur la cybersécurité, contre 63% en 2024.
« Si les Français semblent toujours mieux identifier les cybermalveillances, les résultats 2026 montrent à l’opposé que, face à ces menaces, les besoins d’accompagnement augmentent », déclare Jérôme Notin.
Pour répondre à ce besoin d’informations, Cybermalveillance a prévu une série d’actions d’envergure, à commencer par une grande campagne nationale de sensibilisation, dans le cadre du Cybermois. Il s’agit d’une opération annuelle de sensibilisation à la cybersécurité, qui s’inscrit dans le Cybersecurity Month européen, qui se déroule chaque année en octobre.
Alors que les fuites de données se multiplient dans l’Hexagone, la France enchaîne les ripostes. Après avoir interpellé l’un des cybercriminels à l’origine des violations de l’été, l’Hexagone a demandé à des ingénieurs de Mistral d’utiliser l’IA pour améliorer les systèmes de sécurité de ses ministères. Par ailleurs, Sébastien Lecornu a demandé à ses ministres un « sursaut sur le volet cyber » en prenant des mesures fortes avant la fin du mois de septembre.

articles.title: Para Zuckerberg, la seguridad de la IA no es un freno: es el argumento de venta contra Anthropic y OpenAI
articles.text:
Las empresas de IA están "jugando con nuestras vidas". Es lo que dijo Jacob Coxon, exingeniero de Anthropic justo después de abandonar la compañía. Lo que le siguió fue un terremoto que ha puesto patas arriba la industria de la IA. De un lado tenemos a los responsables de las empresas de IA, con Dario Amodei al frente, abogan por echar el freno y ralentizar el desarrollo ante un inminente riesgo para la humanidad. Del otro lado tenemos a Trump y Jensen Huang, que quieren justo lo contrario: acelerar. Había un líder tecnológico que aún no se había pronunciado: Mark Zuckerberg.
Zuck ha hablado. En un mensaje publicado en su cuenta de X, el CEO de Meta se ha pronunciado sobre la polémica de estos días, criticando de forma indirecta el discurso de Anthropic y OpenAI: "Cada laboratorio tiene la responsabilidad y el incentivo para avanzar al ritmo necesario para entrenar sus modelos de manera segura". Zuckerberg no niega que existan riesgos, pero rechaza una pausa coordinada para toda la industria y traslada la responsabilidad de crear productos seguros directamente a los laboratorios. Además, les recuerda que los laboratorios "enfrentan una responsabilidad legal significativa si sus modelos causan daño".
La alineación no es secundaria. Para Zuckerberg, la seguridad y alineación de los modelos no es algo secundario, sino primordial en el desarrollo de la IA. La propuesta encabezada por Amodei es ralentizar el desarrollo para permitir que la seguridad consiga ponerse al mismo nivel. Zuckerberg es claro ahí: "Mi opinión es que la confianza y la alineación se están convirtiendo rápidamente en las capacidades más importantes que diferenciarán a los agentes y modelos. Cualquier laboratorio que no se enfoque en la alineación se quedará atrás".
Automejora no, gracias. Zuckerberg también ha criticado la carrera por la llamada automejora recursiva de la IA, es decir, que los modelos logren mejorarse a sí mismos. En su opinión, los laboratorios no deberían estar enfocando gran parte del cómputo en esto, sino en "servir a las personas" porque es "una de las mejores formas de asegurar que desarrollemos esta tecnología de manera segura". Es una crítica indirecta, pero bastante clara, a la creación de una superinteligencia que Anthropic ha puesto en el centro de su argumentario.
Meta ya lo hace. Zuckerberg no ha perdido la oportunidad de destacar que Meta ya está cumpliendo con todas esas acciones que propone Amodei. Asegura que retrasaron el lanzamiento de su modelo Muse "durante varios meses para enfocarse en la seguridad y la protección" y añade que "No pedimos que todos los demás lo hicieran. Simplemente lo hicimos como parte de nuestro trabajo diario porque claramente era lo correcto para las personas y para nosotros". Esto es claramente un dardo contra el discurso de Amodei, que pide que todos paren a la vez y se cree un marco regulatorio en torno a esto.
El CEO de Meta también destaca que su empresa ya integra evaluadores y asesores independientes "en varias áreas porque ayuda a producir un mejor trabajo", y suelta otro dardo: "Otros laboratorios simplemente pueden hacer esto también".
Son su competencia. Que Zuckerberg no se alinee con OpenAI y Anthropic tiene todo el sentido desde el punto de vista competitivo. La compañía ha hecho grandes esfuerzos para recortar distancia con su competencia, empezando por el fichaje de numerosos ingenieros e investigadores a los que ofrecieron sueldos de locura. Meta ya ha lanzado su modelo de IA Muse Spark, un agente personal y se espera que en las próximas semanas haya un nuevo lanzamiento, según el New York Times. Se habla de un modelo al que internamente se refieren como Watermelon, y será el más potente que han hecho hasta la fecha.

articles.title: The US just admitted, for the first time, that it has weapons deployed in space
articles.text:
Why it matters: The idea of militarizing outer space is as old as the space race itself, but the US has not openly admitted to deploying weapons beyond Earth's atmosphere until now. While the confirmation was likely intended as a deterrent, the effectiveness of the Air Force secretary's vague statement remains unclear.
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said at a Monday event that the US has deployed weapons in orbit to defend against hostile action. The admission crosses a new boundary following decades of peaceful international competition and cooperation in space.
Meink did not specify the nature of the weapons, according to CNN. However, the statement, made at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference in Maryland, remains significant because it represents a major shift in the US's posture toward outer space.
The declaration is likely aimed at China and Russia, which the US has long accused of developing and potentially testing military applications that could threaten orbital infrastructure. However, as a deterrent, its impact could be limited because other countries still lack a clear idea of the US's destructive capabilities in space.
While the statement is significant, it likely does not violate space law. The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 prohibits deploying nuclear weapons or other weapons of mass destruction in orbit but does not explicitly forbid conventional weapons.
Currently, the most viable theoretical space weapons would aim to neutralize communication satellites by jamming or destroying them. For example, Russia has previously warned that satellites supporting the defense of Ukraine, such as those used by Starlink, would be considered legitimate military targets. Late last year, intelligence services from two NATO countries claimed that Russia is developing a method of attacking satellites using clouds of tiny projectiles orbiting Earth at high velocities, but whether the country could deploy such a weapon remains unclear.
The US Space Force has also accused China of practicing coordinated satellite movements in low Earth orbit that it described as "dogfighting." Meanwhile, one theoretical defensive method might involve stationing a shielded mobile launch platform in orbit.
Outside of military applications, the Moon has once again become a major focus of the space race between countries and private companies. American and European space agencies, along with China, have spent recent years conceptualizing a lunar economy that could involve permanent habitats, data centers, power plants, and other infrastructure.

articles.title: SpaceX prepara para el 22 de septiembre el primer intento de Starship para alcanzar la órbita
articles.text:
SpaceX prepara el decimocuarto vuelo de prueba de Starship para el próximo 22 de septiembre, en una misión que tendrá como principal objetivo intentar que la etapa superior del megacohete alcance la órbita terrestre por primera vez. El lanzamiento tendrá una ventana de 75 minutos que comenzará a las 7:15 horas central de Estados Unidos.
La misión también tendrá una novedad: SpaceX planea desplegar los primeros satélites Starlink de tercera generación (V3) destinados a formar parte de su red de internet. La compañía prevé colocar 26 satélites en órbita durante este vuelo experimental.
PUBLICIDAD
Si el lanzamiento cumple sus objetivos, será un momento relevante para el programa Starship, que SpaceX desarrolla con la intención de convertirlo en su principal vehículo para misiones espaciales y, eventualmente, sustituir a sus actuales Falcon 9 y Falcon Heavy.
Starship intentará llegar a la órbita por primera vez
Hasta ahora, las pruebas de Starship han permitido avanzar en diferentes aspectos del funcionamiento del vehículo, pero la etapa superior todavía no ha conseguido completar una misión orbital.
En el decimotercer vuelo de prueba, realizado en julio, la nave logró realizar un vuelo controlado y completar un aterrizaje simulado en el océano Índico. Aunque no alcanzó la órbita, la etapa superior tuvo un comportamiento suficientemente estable como para no destruirse inmediatamente al entrar en contacto con el agua.
PUBLICIDAD
SpaceX aprovechó esta circunstancia para recuperar la nave y trasladarla lentamente hasta sus instalaciones en Texas. El análisis del vehículo permitió a los ingenieros estudiar los daños y obtener información para introducir nuevas modificaciones antes del próximo lanzamiento.
También habrá cambios en el escudo térmico
Uno de los elementos que SpaceX ha modificado para el vuelo 14 es el escudo térmico de Starship. La compañía asegura que realizó cambios adicionales a partir de lo aprendido durante el análisis de la etapa superior recuperada después del vuelo anterior.
El escudo es fundamental para una futura misión completamente reutilizable, ya que la nave debe soportar las elevadas temperaturas generadas durante su regreso a la atmósfera terrestre.
PUBLICIDAD
En esta ocasión, sin embargo, el objetivo principal será demostrar que la etapa superior puede alcanzar la órbita y completar las maniobras previstas.
SpaceX no intentará recuperar la nave
Aunque la compañía ha trabajado en sistemas para recuperar Starship, esta misión no incluirá uno de los objetivos que se habían planteado anteriormente.
Elon Musk había sugerido que SpaceX podría intentar utilizar la torre de lanzamiento para atrapar la etapa superior después de su regreso. Sin embargo, el empresario descartó recientemente esa posibilidad al considerar que una eventual explosión podría representar un contratiempo demasiado importante para el programa en este momento.
El Super Heavy, el enorme propulsor utilizado durante el despegue, tampoco será recuperado durante este vuelo. SpaceX ha introducido varias modificaciones en su hardware y software después de detectar problemas durante el vuelo 13.
PUBLICIDAD
Uno de los principales inconvenientes estuvo relacionado con el reinicio de los motores del propulsor después de la separación de Starship. Para el próximo lanzamiento, la compañía asegura haber realizado otra ronda de cambios destinada a solucionar los problemas identificados.
Los primeros Starlink V3 llegarán al espacio
El vuelo 14 también servirá para poner en órbita 26 satélites Starlink V3, una generación diseñada para ampliar las capacidades de la red de internet de SpaceX.
En el vuelo anterior, la empresa ya había utilizado Starship para desplegar satélites V3, pero aquellos vehículos tenían un objetivo principalmente experimental y terminaron desintegrándose en la atmósfera aproximadamente 20 minutos después.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta vez, SpaceX pretende que los satélites formen parte de su infraestructura orbital. Si se completa el despliegue previsto, será además la primera misión de Starship que genere ingresos para la división de lanzamientos de SpaceX, aunque los clientes pertenecen a otra división de la misma compañía.
Un paso clave para el futuro de Starship
SpaceX ha invertido miles de millones de dólares en el desarrollo de Starship y busca que el vehículo pueda realizar lanzamientos frecuentes y reutilizarse rápidamente.
El objetivo declarado por Musk es llegar a un ritmo de varios vuelos semanales, algo que permitiría a la empresa depender menos de los Falcon 9 y Falcon Heavy y concentrar recursos de ingeniería y producción en un único sistema.
PUBLICIDAD
El vuelo del 22 de septiembre todavía no demostrará toda esa capacidad. Primero deberá superar el desafío fundamental de llevar la etapa superior de Starship a la órbita terrestre. El resultado determinará hasta qué punto el programa ha avanzado desde el vuelo anterior y qué nuevos pasos deberá dar SpaceX para convertir su megacohete en un sistema espacial plenamente operativo.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Dropbox Evolves Riviera Content Processing Platform to Support AI Workloads
articles.text:
Dropbox has evolved Riviera from a file preview service into a universal content processing platform supporting more than 300 file formats and more than 100 transformation capabilities. The platform now performs hundreds of thousands of transformations per second and supports Search, Replay, Sign, and Dash, allowing AI workloads to reuse content processing infrastructure developed for earlier products.
Riviera began as an internal service for generating previews across Dropbox's file formats. Instead of creating separate processing services for individual formats and outputs, engineers decomposed content processing into reusable transformations. A PowerPoint preview, for example, can be generated by converting the presentation to PDF and then converting PDF pages into images. These transformations can then be composed into other processing pipelines.
Riviera's composable transformation pipeline (Source: Dropbox Blog Post)
The architecture separates orchestration from execution. A central component validates requests, composes transformation pipelines, dispatches work to backend workers, and manages caching. Individual workers implement specific transformation capabilities, while a plugin model allows new capabilities to be added without changing the core orchestration layer.
Riviera's integration across Dropbox products and core surfaces (Source: Dropbox Blog Post)
Riviera was already being used for AI processing before the latest expansion. Dropbox previously described chaining transformations to convert content into text and embeddings for AI-powered summaries and question answering. At that time, the platform supported roughly 300 file types and processed about 2.5 billion requests per day, representing nearly an exabyte of data. Cached intermediate results allowed multiple AI operations to reuse previously generated content.
Dash introduced additional content preparation requirements because its search and AI capabilities process content from Dropbox and connected services. Riviera provides transformations for extracting and normalizing that content before indexing, allowing Dash to use the existing processing pipeline.
Dropbox has also exposed Riviera capabilities through public APIs. The developer documentation describes asynchronous endpoints for converting documents to Markdown, transcribing audio and video, and extracting structured metadata. The Markdown API supports applications including indexing, rendering, and providing documents as input to large language models. Applications submit jobs and poll using an asynchronous job identifier, with completion and failure states returned separately.
The platform is also appearing in external developer tooling. A developer in the Dropbox Community published conductor-dropbox, an open source integration for Conductor OSS and Orkes that includes asynchronous Riviera Markdown extraction for document and RAG workflows. The project combines Dropbox operations with workflow orchestration for document and AI processing.
Riviera differs from general-purpose extraction frameworks such as Apache Tika, which provides APIs for detecting, parsing, and extracting text and metadata from a broad range of file formats. Riviera combines transformation plugins with pipeline composition, asynchronous execution, caching, and centralized orchestration.
Dropbox is now exposing selected Riviera capabilities through APIs while continuing to use the platform across document, multimedia, search, and AI workloads. The external Conductor integration provides an example of Riviera's content extraction capabilities being incorporated into a broader workflow orchestration system.

articles.title: AI minister affirms Canada will have tech super-regulator “with teeth” | BetaKit
articles.text:
Amid global concerns over AI safety, Canada’s AI minister reaffirmed that the country’s proposed “super-regulator” for digital technology will have the power to hold companies accountable to the sum of billions.
The news: AI and digital innovation minister Evan Solomon made the remarks on Wednesday morning at the ALL IN AI conference in Montréal. Alongside promises of a robust regulator, Solomon teased that the federal government will reveal which organization will build Canada’s public AI supercomputer “early this fall.”
From the source: “We are setting up to do all this—a regulator with teeth—for the first time in Canadian history,” Solomon said. “Not just a regulator that can name and shame, but that can hold these big tech companies to account if they are abusive, with billions of dollars in fines.”
The context: As part of a long-awaited update to Canada’s privacy law, Solomon proposed the creation of a regulator known as the Canadian Digital Safety Commission. It would have a broad mandate, including oversight of privacy issues in the private sector and the implementation of the new Safe Social Media Act.
If that bill becomes law, the new regulator would be able to issue binding orders and monetary penalties of up to $10 million, or three percent of global revenue, which is a departure from the powers of Canada’s existing privacy regulator.
Final thought: While this “super-regulator” could hold US AI developers accountable in the digital sphere, it’s less clear how Canada will deal with the associated AI buildout. Earlier this month, the Canadian government released a basic data centre framework which asks, but doesn’t mandate, companies to follow responsible development guidelines. For data centres, he said that provincial regulators can create rules with “more legislative teeth.”
Feature image courtesy Evan Solomon via X.

articles.title: The Specialized Diverge Pro 4 makes rough gravel your playground
articles.text:
When I make my yearly trip to Denver, I always bring my road bike. It’s my annual chance to suffer on the kinds of gradients unavailable in the glacier-scoured lands of northeastern Illinois. In advance of this year’s trip, Specialized hooked me up with its new gravel bike, the Diverge Pro 4, so I brought it with me to challenge it in ways not possible on the fastidiously groomed gravel trails of suburban Chicago.
In contrast to the Specialized Turbo Creo 2 we reviewed a couple of years ago, the Diverge Pro 4 is strictly human-powered. Specialized calls it “the ultimate getaway vehicle,” designed with input from off-road adventure riders, scientists, and racers. It’s marketed as the only gravel bike you need for racing, adventure, and distance rides. While I can’t speak to its racing performance, I can say the Diverge Pro 4 is a blast on any kind of gravel and does well enough on the road.
Priced at $8,249, the Diverge Pro 4 is designed for rough trails and technical descents, both of which unfolded below me at the summit of an is-it-gravel-or-is-it-single-track climb in Douglas County, Colorado. I took a deep breath, and down I went. The descent was rutted and slightly more technical than anything I’ll ever run into around Chicago, but I had enough time on the bike to realize that if I had trouble on the descent, it wouldn’t be the bike’s fault.
A “shocking” update
To understand what makes the Diverge Pro 4 stand out, I’ll start with my favorite feature. Future Shock 3.3 is Specialized’s suspension system, and it’s a significant upgrade over the earlier versions used on the Turbo Creo 2 and Diverge Pro 3. The mechanism lives between the head tube and stem. It isolates the rider from high-frequency impacts while adding relatively little weight and without changing the bike’s steering geometry or introducing brake dive—two compromises that can come with conventional suspension forks. The fork, head tube, and front wheel remain rigidly connected, with the stem and handlebars moving vertically relative to the rest of the bike.
Future Shock uses hydraulic damping to control the movement of the spring inside the head tube. A spring by itself will just compress and return the stored energy, which can lead to a pogo-stick-like experience on bumpy roads and gravel. The damper converts some of that energy into heat by forcing fluid through a controlled pathway. The result on nasty terrain is controlled vertical movement rather than a bouncy rebound. 20 mm doesn’t sound like much, especially to anyone accustomed to mountain bikes with 100 mm or more of suspension travel. But Future Shock isn’t trying to keep a wheel planted while you launch off a rock. Its job is to prevent a stream of smaller impacts from traveling through the handlebars, into your hands, arms, shoulders, and eventually your increasingly annoyed brain. And it’s very good at it.
Specialized says laboratory testing showed up to a 53 percent reduction in peak impact at the bars versus competing setups. That’s an impressively precise number generated under equally precise laboratory conditions, so don’t read it as “every bump feels 53 percent smaller.” But whatever the decrease, the underlying effect wasn’t difficult to detect, as I felt less arm and upper-body fatigue after long rides than I experience on my own gravel bike.
Compression damping can be adjusted on the fly with a dial at the top of the stem, changing how readily the system moves through its 20 mm of travel. At the firmest setting, Future Shock moves very little under normal riding loads; open it up, and the bars move much more freely over bumps. After some experimentation, I left it fully open on nearly every surface.
Specialized made a number of other changes from the Diverge Pro 3, all of which are positives in my book. The Diverge Pro 4 sports the bike maker’s mid-range FACT 9r carbon frame with reworked geometry that offers longer reach for better weight centering. With the bottom bracket sitting 5 mm lower, the rider’s center of gravity is lower, contributing to a more planted feel in corners. All told, the Diverge Pro 4 weighs in at 8.72 kg.
The Specialized Diverge Pro 4 at rest.
Eric Bangeman
The Specialized Diverge Pro 4 at rest.
Eric Bangeman
Paired with the 40-tooth chainring, the 13-speed SRAM Force cassette is up for any terrain.
Eric Bangeman
Paired with the 40-tooth chainring, the 13-speed SRAM Force cassette is up for any terrain.
Eric Bangeman
The Specialized Diverge Pro 4 at rest.
Eric Bangeman
Paired with the 40-tooth chainring, the 13-speed SRAM Force cassette is up for any terrain.
Eric Bangeman
Although the Diverge Pro 4 comes with 45 mm tires, there’s more than enough clearance for 50 mm tires—in fact, the Diverge I reviewed came with a set of 50 mm Terra TLR Trail gravel tires mounted on the tubeless-ready Roval Terra CL carbon wheelset.
The Diverge Pro’s drivetrain is the SRAM Force XPLR E1, which comes with a single 40t chainring; a 13-speed, 10–46 cassette; and programmable bonus buttons on the brake hoods. It’s a fantastic groupset, offering the same features as the pricier SRAM Red drivetrain in a slightly heavier, less-expensive package. The rear derailleur mounts to a replaceable Universal Derailleur Hanger, or UDH, which means a bent hanger is easier to replace than a proprietary one (which is better than finishing a long ride with limited shifting after you bit it on a corner because you didn’t see some loose gravel and bent your derailleur hanger… not that I’d know anything about that). I found the gear ratios to be more than adequate for anything outside of dropping the hammer on a flat segment of smooth tarmac, and I really appreciated the gearing on climbs while laboring up steep gradients on the big sprocket. I even had an occasion to take advantage of the massive 46t cog in back on a particularly steep stretch of road.
There’s also a Quarq Power Meter tucked away inside the spindle, which measures watts generated on the left side to calculate total power output.
The Diverge Pro 4 keeps the downtube storage area from the 3, and it’s larger. That means more room for a spare inner tube, CO2 cartridges, and tools for in-ride repairs. Or snacks, but I prefer a top-tube bag for gels, Skittles, and other on-bike munching.
A lesson in compliance
To make it to the nearest gravel trail, I need to ride a couple of miles of surface streets, so let’s briefly talk about riding the Diverge Pro 4 on pavement. It’s fine. With the DT350 hubs and bumpy 50 mm tires, the bike sounded like I was powering up a dynamo with each rotation of the pedals. The Diverge feels decidedly stolid on pavement, favoring comfort and stability over the liveliness of a road bike.
The 3D-printed saddle with cutout felt just right.
Eric Bangeman
The 3D-printed saddle with cutout felt just right.
Eric Bangeman
The dial at the top of the stem adjusts the amount of damping.
The dial at the top of the stem adjusts the amount of damping.
I programmed the bonus buttons on the brake hoods to move between screens on my Garmin bike computer.
Eric Bangeman
I programmed the bonus buttons on the brake hoods to move between screens on my Garmin bike computer.
Eric Bangeman
The dial at the top of the stem adjusts the amount of damping.
I programmed the bonus buttons on the brake hoods to move between screens on my Garmin bike computer.
Eric Bangeman
Gravel is where the Diverge Pro 4 shines.
It didn’t matter whether I was cruising down a smoothly groomed, crushed-limestone path winding along the Des Plaines River or barreling down a washboard of a gravel road in the foothills of the Rockies. The Diverge gobbled up every surface I threw at it, giving me more confidence to attack stretches of chunky gravel and a feeling of stability on descents—even the technical ones. Whether you’re on rough country roads, flowy singletrack, or bikepacking, the Diverge can handle it.
I’m not a fan of the MTB bottle cage, but the tool storage compartment is a nice feature.
Credit:
Eric Bangeman
I’m not a fan of the MTB bottle cage, but the tool storage compartment is a nice feature.
Credit:
Eric Bangeman
There’s not much to dislike about the Diverge Pro 4. The Quarq DUB-PWR meter estimates total wattage from the left leg alone; I’d prefer a spider-based meter that measures total power at the crank spider rather than extrapolating from one side. The cranks on the 56 cm Diverge are 172.5 mm, which is out of step with an industry trend toward shorter cranks. After my second right knee replacement, I swapped out the 172.5 mm cranks on my road bike for 165 mm. Getting into an aero posture is easier and more comfortable with shorter cranks, and since my knees don’t go as high at the 12 o’clock position, there’s less hip impingement, and I experience less discomfort overall. I’m also not a fan of the mountain bike-style S-Works Carbon Zee bottle cage with the openings on the side. I ride with one-liter bottles on hot days, and my leg would occasionally bump the bottle lid on the open side of the cage.
But those are truly minor quibbles. Ultimately, the Diverge Pro 4 is a fantastic gravel bike that is ideal for those who love rough gravel, long rides, or bikepacking through the wilderness. But let’s be frank: Not everyone needs to ride around on an $8,000 gravel bike—if you would be happy with a less-expensive aluminum bike or carbon setup with a mechanical groupset, this isn’t the bike for you. (And if your wallet is wide open, Specialized just launched the $12,500 S-Works Diverge Pro this week.) But if you’re more Unbound Gravel than groomed gravel, you can’t go wrong with the Diverge Pro 4.
Eric Bangeman is the Managing Editor of Ars Technica. He lives in the northwest suburbs of Chicago, where he enjoys road cycling and plays bass in a band.

articles.title: Watch out — TP-Link Tapo Camera vulnerabilities could let hackers spy inside homes, so patch now
articles.text:
Watch out — TP-Link Tapo Camera vulnerabilities could let hackers spy inside homes, so patch now
Researchers find two flaws in highly popular cameras
- Opswat found two flaws in TP‑Link Tapo C200 cameras: auth bypass (CVE‑2026‑15315) and DoS (CVE‑2026‑15316)
- Bugs let attackers hijack admin sessions or crash devices; millions of users potentially exposed
- TP‑Link patched with firmware V5_1.4.6 on Aug 18, 2026; users urged to update immediately
Security researchers found a pair of vulnerabilities in popular smart cameras, which could allow threat actors to peep into people’s homes and businesses.
Earlier this week, Opswat disclosed finding two bugs in the TP-Link Tapo C200 smart security camera - an authentication bypass flaw, and a denial-of-service vulnerability. The former is tracked as CVE-2026-15315 and was given a severity score of 8.7/10 (high). Opswat says the bug allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain valid admin sessions without having a password, which would allow them to manage the device and even watch the stream.
The latter is tracked as CVE-2026-15316. With a severity score of 7.1/10 (high), this bug allows threat actors to send oversized crypted ciphertext values that may trigger exception handling failures and cause the affected device to crash or restart. “Successful exploitation may temporarily disrupt HTTPS management and monitoring functionality, resulting in a denial-of-service (DoS) condition until the service recovers,” according to the NVD.
Patching the bugs
The C200 is a mass-market product, advertised as a security camera, a baby monitor, or a pet camera, with motion detection, 1080p video, 2-way audio, night vision, cloud & SD card storage, and integrations with both Alexa and Google Home.
Opswat disclosed their findings to TP-Link in mid-April this year, which started working on a fix in early July this year. On August 18, 2026, TP-Link released firmware version V5_1.4.6, which addressed both flaws. Users are advised to install the fix as soon as possible.
The researchers did not discuss if the flaws were being abused in the wild, or to what extent. We do know that TP-Link Tapo cameras are rather popular, with the C200 model being relatively widely sold. According to TP-Link, the Tapo app has more than 13 million users, while the Google Play Store shows 10+ million downloads.
On Amazon, the C200 specifically is listed as the #1 top rated product in its category, with more than 3,000 purchases this month alone.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"Camera bugs always get attention because of the "spy factor," but they usually sound cooler and scarier than they actually are," said Dahvid Schloss, OSCP, Chief Operating Officer at Suzu Labs. "The main reason not to "worry" about this one is that running this exploit requires local network access, so a threat actor has to be on your Wi-Fi or already own a device that is.
"If someone's made it that far into your network, they're not after the baby monitor. Now, if the camera was port-forwarded to the internet, that's a bigger design issue and probably should be a concern, but not a common setup for the everyday home user. Either way, I'd still patch the camera, but it's pretty low on the totem pole of what a cybercriminal wants."
"I'm quite curious about the undisclosed vulnerability that reportedly allows full compromise and a foothold to pivot from," Schloss added. "Based on what was reported, I would guess the exploit would be a command injection or a memory-safety bug in the same management service, chained behind that auth bypass to get code execution as root, where they then dropped a static binary to return a shell on the device whose firmware ships with almost no tooling. That attack chain isn't uncommon on cheap, older consumer IoT devices where security wasn't top of mind, but if that's the case here, seeing it hold up on a modern TP-Link device would be a bit of a blast from the past.

articles.title: ¿Revive el Xserve? Apple volvería a fabricar servidores para aprovechar el furor por la IA
articles.text:
Apple podría volver a fabricar servidores para terceros, aprovechando el furor por la inteligencia artificial generativa. Según reporta The Information, los de Cupertino verían con buenos ojos la posibilidad de regresar al mercado de hardware de grado empresarial, que alguna vez supo animar de la mano de la línea Xserve.
De acuerdo con el citado medio, Apple todavía no ha tomado una decisión final respecto de su posible regreso al mundo de los servidores. Pero si avanza con este plan, el primer modelo de la potencial nueva línea se haría esperar unos años antes de hacer su debut en el mercado.
La información disponible señala que Apple podría reaparecer en el mercado de servidores para terceros a partir de 2029. El reporte indica que el equipo podría ser impulsado por dos o cuatro chips M8 Ultra, dependiendo de las configuraciones que se pongan a disposición de los compradores.
Apple lleva tiempo desarrollando sus propios servidores de uso interno, basados en los chips Apple Silicon que impulsan los Mac actuales. Sin embargo, hasta aquí nunca ha ofrecido la posibilidad de que terceros los adquieran para uso propio. Si lo que se reporta es certero, la historia podría cambiar en los próximos años gracias al furor por la inteligencia artificial generativa, siempre voraz de poder de cómputo.
Todavía no se sabe si el reingreso de Apple al mundo de los servidores se dará con la reaparición de la vieja marca Xserve, o si la conducción de John Ternus buscará diferenciarse de los esfuerzos del pasado con una denominación totalmente nueva.
Apple podría volver a fabricar servidores, más de 15 años después de matar los Xserve
Un dato interesante que revela The Information es que Apple se habría puesto en contacto con NVIDIA para adoptar su tecnología en sus presuntos nuevos servidores. Más específicamente, el sistema NVLink que permite conectar varios chips para que funcionen como si se tratara de uno solo.
Si las conversaciones entre ambas compañías avanzan, podría darle aún más fuerza a una alianza ya existente. Tengamos en cuenta que los de Cupertino han utilizado hardware de NVIDIA en los servidores que impulsan a Siri AI, de modo que una colaboración más profunda no sería una rareza. Además, estamos hablando de las dos empresas más valiosas del mundo, por lo que un trabajo en conjunto seguramente tendría buena repercusión en el mercado bursátil.
Apple hizo varios intentos en el mundo de los servidores empresariales durante su historia, principalmente durante los años noventa y la primera década del 2000. El más recordado es el Xserve, que debutó en 2002 y se mantuvo en su catálogo en 2011, cuando se optó por su discontinuación.
Las primeras dos generaciones de estos servidores de Apple fueron impulsadas por chips PowerPC G4 y G5, mientras que la tercera se benefició de la transición a Intel con la adopción de los procesadores Xeon. A finales de 2010, los de la manzana anunciaron que ya no continuarían produciendo nuevas versiones, poniendo punto y final al producto a principios de 2011. A partir de entonces, la compañía recomendó la migración a alternativas como el Mac mini Server o el Mac Pro Server como reemplazo a sus servidores en rack.

articles.title: Microsoft to hold Oct. 7 Windows and Surface event
articles.text:
Microsoft announced that it’s hosting an event in San Francisco, California, on Oct. 7, specifically about “how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC.”
Although the company hasn’t shared many details about the event, it looks likely that it will focus on Surface Laptops. It could be where we learn more about the previously announced Surface Laptop Ultra sporting Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip.
Further supporting that notion, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Microsoft Executive Vice President of Windows and Devices, Pavan Davuluri, are expected to attend.
Per Engadget, Microsoft says the three will share details on Windows, RTX Spark, Surface, and the broader PC ecosystem. So it seems very likely the Oct. 7 event will feature the Surface Laptop Ultra. Further, we could see other RTX Spark laptops at the event, similar to how Microsoft unveiled its Copilot Plus PC line-up with Surface devices and laptops from several third-party manufacturers back in 2024.
Nvidia first announced the RTX Spark chip back in June at Computex in Taipei, Taiwan. The company called Spark the “most efficient PC chip ever built” and claimed it would be capable of rendering massive 3D scenes, editing 12K video, and running large language models (LLMs) locally.
Naturally, gaming was also a big factor for Nvidia, which claimed that Spark can handle AAA games at 1440p resolution at 100+ frames per second (fps) with ray tracing enabled. Of course, that notably relies on DLSS software for upscaling, which likely means it’s not running at true 1440p and therefore isn’t as impressive as Nvidia would like you to believe.
There are still a lot of unknowns about the RTX Spark chip and the Surface Laptop Ultra, as well as the other laptops that are expected to sport this new chipset.
Back in June, we learned that alongside the Surface line, there would be laptops from Asus, MSI, Dell, HP, Lenovo, and more sporting Spark. We don’t yet know if any of these will be at the Microsoft event, but I suspect we’ll see them.

articles.title: 'Defeated' GPT-6 Astra model spent several hours just farming potatoes after being blown up by a Creeper in Minecraft — OpenAI offering gets further than any other AI system in 141-hour test
articles.text:
'Defeated' GPT-6 Astra model spent several hours just farming potatoes after being blown up by a Creeper in Minecraft — OpenAI offering gets further than any other AI system in 141-hour test
They're just like us...
An apparently sad and defeated GPT-6 Astra spent several hours doing nothing but farming potatoes during a 141-hour Minecraft benchmark test, after dying and losing all of its gear to an exploding Creeper. Vals AI records that while GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's latest frontier model, got further than any AI system had in its 141-hour test, the experiment did reveal a distinctly human lapse in motivation after all of its progress was wiped out by the destructive mob.
While the model outclassed rivals in how much it was able to achieve, the test has gone viral for a different reason. After Astra put all of its valuable end-game items in a chest, a Creeper appeared and blew up both the chest and Astra's bed — a calamity any Minecraft player will tell you is the worst thing that can happen. Not only did Astra lose all of the items to the explosion, but the bed destruction wiped the spawn point out, effectively resetting your game progress to zero. "Here, the most expensive creeper explosion occurred. Later, on a coincidentally rainy day, Astra discovers it lost everything. It all went downhill from here," Vals records.
"The model appeared defeated, spending the next several hours doing essentially nothing but farming potatoes," Vals observed. In fact, it got so bad that viewers on Twitch watching the experiment live started to agitate for the model to pick up the pace. Like all good Minecraft players, Astra reportedly became "paranoid about creepers," logging "GREEN tall thing ahead was SUGARCANE, NOT creeper!"
The AI was also recorded berating itself for dropping things, and even warned itself, "do NOT waste another night chasing dark pink pixels," i.e., pigs.
Astra has made waves as OpenAI's latest frontier model, which is notably adept thanks to its computer use and browsing, letting it navigate, click, and type like a human using a computer. The company has claimed it's an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities. Last week, the model was recorded autonomously completing Portal in just 24 hours at a cost of just $571 in tokens.

articles.title: Co-founder Max Hodak joins the agenda lineup on Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When you imagine working with a computer, you likely think of keyboards, clicks, or typing on your phone. Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak has spent the last several months advancing a different vision. His company has enlisted a top neurobiologist to lead the first U.S. human trials for its biohybrid brain-computer interface. Hodak shares what his company has discovered so far with the 10,000+ tech leaders, founders, and investors at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.
At his Beyond Screens session on the Disrupt Stage, Hodak will make the case for why the next era of technology could be built upon a different kind of interface, one that adapts to us from brain-computer interactions to create new ways of engaging with machines.
Join Disrupt as it returns to Moscone West in San Francisco on October 13-15, bringing together more than 10,000 founders, investors, and startup community members across more than 250 sessions. This year, we have a particular focus on building sustainable AI companies, with AI-centric programming extending across six industry stages.
Secure your Disrupt pass today to save up to $200 on your ticket and hear one of Silicon Valley’s most ambitious founders explore a post-screen future.
Hodak’s path toward reinventing interfaces
Hodak’s career reads like a running bet that the interface between humans and machines has plenty of room for improvement. Having started programming at six years old, he studied biomedical engineering at Duke Pratt School of Engineering, and worked his way into Miguel Nicolelis’ brain-computer interface lab, interests that inform his work to this day.
He originally co-founded Transcriptic, a robotic cloud laboratory for the life sciences. But most famously, he co-founded Neuralink in 2016 and served as its initial president, helping build the company that put brain implants into the public imagination. Then in 2021, he founded Science Corporation to develop advanced neural engineering and brain-computer interface technology. The company has a particular focus on applications to aid those in need of help with vision, cognition, and mobility.
And it’s not all speculation: Science Corp’s PRIMA implant has already restored eyesight in people with severe vision loss, using a pair of glasses with a tiny camera that beams a captured scene onto a chip implanted in the retina. Since its founding, it’s raised $230 million in a Series C round at a $1.5 billion valuation, and the company’s ambitions go beyond interfaces. Hodak sees additional applications of Science Corp’s brain-implanted sensors helping heal damaged brain cells, warning about seizures, and maybe even helping treat conditions as severe as Parkinson’s disease.
Hear from one of Silicon Valley’s most ambitious founders, only at Disrupt
This is your best chance to learn how Hodak thinks the interface between people and machines is about to change, and the many ways that could impact your startup, your role, and maybe your life.

articles.title: Réparer la batterie plutôt que la changer : le spécialiste EV Clinic ouvre son premier atelier en France
articles.text:
EV Clinic s’est fait connaître en Europe en réparant des batteries que les constructeurs jugent bonnes à être remplacées. Le spécialiste de la réparation de voitures électriques a ouvert ce mardi 15 septembre 2026 son premier atelier français, au sud de Paris. Pour un propriétaire dont la garantie a expiré, c’est une alternative au passage quasi obligé par la concession.
Fondée à Zagreb, en Croatie, EV Clinic répare depuis plusieurs années des composants que la plupart des garages ne touchent pas : batteries haute tension, moteurs électriques, onduleurs, chargeurs embarqués. Après l’Allemagne, la Slovénie et la Serbie, la firme a jeté son dévolu sur la France. EV Clinic n’arrive pas sur un terrain vierge : un réseau comme Revolte, lancé à Nantes en 2022, entretient déjà des électriques et hybrides en Île-de-France.
Ouvrir la batterie plutôt que la changer
Quand une batterie présente un défaut, le réseau constructeur lit un code, constate un pack déséquilibré et peut souvent facturer le remplacement complet, ce qui se traduit par une addition à cinq chiffres. C’est là tout le problème que l’enseigne dit vouloir régler. EV Clinic ouvre le pack batterie, mesure chaque cellule et ne remplace que celles qui ont lâché, pour une fraction de la facture constructeur. Le spécialiste avait notamment remis en état la batterie d’une Renault Zoé de 2015 pour 900 euros, quand Renault en réclamait 18 000 pour un pack neuf.
Dans une publication sur son compte X, le spécialiste a également interpellé les propriétaires de Tesla Model 3 Propulsion et Model Y Propulsion pour un problème sur les silentblocs du moteur. Ces caoutchoucs qui absorbent les mouvements peuvent se détériorer au-delà de 100 000 km. EV Clinic propose ce type de réparations préventives, à un coût inférieur à celui facturé par Tesla.
En revanche, sortir du réseau constructeur a un prix. Il est bon de rappeler qu’une réparation menée par un tiers n’offre pas les mêmes garanties qu’un passage en concession, et peut compliquer la prise en charge d’un problème ultérieur. Pour une voiture encore sous garantie, l’atelier indépendant a donc peu d’intérêt. Il vaut mieux faire jouer la couverture du constructeur tant qu’elle est encore valable.
L’offre vise surtout les propriétaires d’électriques vieillissantes et hors garantie, face à un devis de remplacement qui dépasse parfois la valeur de la voiture. Pour eux, réparer la batterie cellule par cellule peut faire la différence entre garder l’auto et l’abandonner.

articles.title: L Catterton to invest in restaurant chain Nandhana Foods
articles.text:
L Catterton to invest in restaurant chain Nandhana Foods
The funding by global consumer focused investment firm L Catterton is expected to support Nandhana Foods' next phase of growth.
Global consumer-focused investment firm L Catterton has entered into a definitive agreement to invest in Nandhana Foods, a leading restaurant group specialising in South Indian cuisine. The value of the investment was not disclosed.
According to a statement, the investment will support Nandhana Foods’ next phase of growth and enable the group to achieve greater scale by leveraging L Catterton’s industry expertise and operating capabilities.
L Catterton Partner Vikram Kumaraswamy said, “Nandhana Foods’ founding family has built a distinctive and scalable business with a strong consumer proposition and attractive unit economics. It has expanded the business in a disciplined manner and ensured that its restaurants remain anchored in high quality and consistency.”
He also said, “We believe there is significant headroom for additional growth by further deepening and broadening its presence in South India and penetrating other markets. There is a clear path for prudently ramping up expansion.”
Founded in 2004, Nandhana Foods is a restaurant group that specialises in Andhra and Karnataka cuisine. It operates two brands, Nandhana Palace and RNR, and has 25 branches across Bengaluru and Chennai.
Nandhana Foods Founder and Managing Director R Ravichandar said, “We are pleased to partner with L Catterton, which has a track record of creating value for its portfolio companies across the world. The firm has a profound grasp of our organisational DNA and an intricate understanding of the restaurant industry.”
The statement said L Catterton has significant experience in building restaurant brands across the world.
The firm has invested in around 30 restaurant businesses till date. Its current and past portfolio companies include Dishoom, P.F. Chang’s, Velvet Taco, Baja Fresh, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen, Cigierre, HUGE, Impresario, and Mendocino Farms.
Founded in 1989, L Catterton manages around $40 billion of equity capital across multi-product platforms dedicated to private equity, credit, and real estate. It has made over 300 investments in consumer brands across the world.

articles.title: Iranian hackers use CHOSEN BRICK Windows malware to spy on targets
articles.text:
Government agencies are warning that Iranian state-linked hackers are using a Windows malware strain named CHOSEN BRICK to target dissidents, activists, and journalists worldwide.
The malware features data theft and espionage capabilities that collect email, Telegram, and WhatsApp communications, take screenshots, and record audio.
The threat actor primarily targeted individuals in the U.S., U.K., and the Netherlands, whose cybersecurity agencies published a joint advisory with the FBI.
A typical attack begins with social engineering messages impersonating trusted contacts or technical support agents, sent to targets via WhatsApp or Telegram.
The threat actor tricks victims into opening malicious files disguised as legitimate applications (e.g., Pictory, RunwayML, Norton Antivirus, Telegram, Adobe Flash Player, KeePass), often suggesting they launch them on personal devices to bypass corporate security blocks.
Depending on the pretext used, the hackers sometimes used even medical-related lures, the agencies found.
The apps display a convincing interface that matches the lure, while silently installing CHOSEN BRICK in the background and securing persistence through Windows Registry Run keys.
The malware adds Microsoft Defender exclusions to evade detection and connects to a unique Telegram bot that matches the victim’s ID and provides command-and-control (C2).
Once launched, CHOSEN BRICK can perform the following actions:
- Collect system information
- Enumerate running processes
- Capture screenshots
- Record audio through the microphone
- Steal email content
- Steal Telegram or WhatsApp browser data
- Download additional payloads to “C:\Windows \SysWOW64”
- Delete files
- Wipe the entire host system
The stolen data is exfiltrated through Telegram or cloud services like VultrObjects and StorjShare, while newer CHOSEN BRICK variants route traffic through SOCKS5 proxies to conceal the activity.
The advisory notes that the stolen data sometimes ends up on pro-Iranian leak sites, serving as a form of harassment and increasing the physical risk for dissidents abroad.
“Iran almost certainly uses cyber activity to support the repression of individuals who are seen as a threat to the regime, such as dissidents, activists and journalists,” the government agencies say.
“In some cases, the Iranian intelligence services have plotted to kidnap or conduct lethal operations against individuals internationally, who they perceive as enemies of the regime.”
Potential victims and organizations should inspect Registry Run entries for suspicious entries, search logs for indicators of compromise (IoCs) shared in the advisory.
Unexpected connections to Telegram’s API, Backblaze B2, VultrObjects, StorjShare, IPRoyal, and LightningProxies should be investigated as suspicious.
Build your security blueprint for AI-powered attacks
Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.
